description: OPD loss taxonomy - 7 mutually exclusive classes used to categorize the loss objective each OPD paper trains with. Granularity is intentionally coarse (matches survey paper §2.3 + KL-only/+RL/+Pref split).

classes.name: Forward KL
classes.what_to_match: Loss is dominated by forward KL where the teacher distribution is the first argument (mode-covering). Includes classical KD with KL(teacher || student), CE-on-teacher-soft-targets when explicitly equivalent.
classes.do_not_match: Pure NLL/CE on hard labels with no teacher distribution. RL with KL(\pi_\theta || \pi_ref) as ref-policy regularizer (that is RKL but NOT teacher distill, route to Other if no teacher).

classes.name: Reverse KL
classes.what_to_match: Loss is dominated by reverse KL where the student distribution is the first argument (mode-seeking). MiniLLM-style policy-gradient interpretations also fall here when the underlying objective is RKL to a teacher.
classes.do_not_match: RKL where teacher slot is occupied by a frozen reference policy of the same model with no teacher signal (that is RL ref-regularization).

classes.name: Symmetric / Skewed KL / JSD / GKL
classes.expression: D_JSD, D_skew-KL_\alpha, D_GKL, or any symmetrized KL combination
classes.what_to_match: Jensen-Shannon divergence; skewed forward/reverse KL with mixture distribution \alpha\pi_T + (1-\alpha)\pi_\theta inside; bidirectional sum a*FKL + b*RKL with both nontrivial; total variation between teacher and student.
classes.do_not_match: Single-direction KL with a small ref-policy regularizer (still FKL or RKL).

classes.name: Other f-divergence (alpha / Renyi / Tsallis / chi-squared)
classes.expression: D_\alpha, D_Renyi, D_chi2, ... (any f-divergence beyond KL/JSD)
classes.what_to_match: Adaptive KL family that interpolates a parameter between FKL and RKL via alpha-divergence (AKL / TAID-style). Renyi divergence. Chi-squared. Tsallis.
classes.do_not_match: Adaptive switching that just toggles between FKL and RKL discretely (route to whichever direction dominates, or Symmetric if mixed).

classes.name: Hybrid KL distill + RL reward
classes.expression: L = D_KL(teacher, student) + \lambda \cdot R(x,a) (or GRPO/PPO surrogate with teacher KL)
classes.what_to_match: Loss explicitly mixes a teacher-KL distillation term with a verifiable reward / advantage / GRPO / PPO surrogate signal. Both terms must be load-bearing (removing either breaks the contribution).
classes.do_not_match: RL-only with ref-policy KL regularizer and no teacher (NOT distillation, route to Other and consider rejection upstream). KL-only paper that uses RL only as a baseline.

classes.name: Preference / Pairwise / DPO-style
classes.expression: DPO-style log-ratio margin between chosen and rejected responses, optionally with a KL-to-teacher hinge
classes.what_to_match: Preference-pair loss is the primary distillation signal: DPO, IPO, SimPO, or preference-gap KL where teacher provides the chosen response and student avoids rejected.
classes.do_not_match: DPO used only as an auxiliary RL term where the main loss is KL distill (route to KL+RL if both load-bearing, FKL/RKL if KL dominates).

classes.name: Other / Bespoke (NLL, MSE, Contrastive, special)
classes.expression: any objective that does not fit the six classes above
classes.what_to_match: MSE on hidden states, contrastive InfoNCE between teacher/student embeddings, NLL on teacher-rolled-out sequences with no KL term, bespoke metric losses.
classes.do_not_match: Any objective whose dominant term is one of the six classes above.

tie_breaking_rules: Pick the SINGLE dominant class. If multiple terms are present, choose the one whose removal would most damage the paper's contribution.
If a paper has both a teacher-KL term and an RL reward and BOTH are load-bearing, pick KL+RL.
If a paper says 'reverse KL' but actually writes D_KL(teacher || student) in the equation, trust the equation.
Self-distillation (no external teacher, but the model itself acts as teacher) still counts as a teacher-distill direction — classify by KL direction.
If only ref-policy KL appears with no teacher distribution (pure RL), classify as Other and flag in notes.
